rubric_items.reason: All five acceptance criteria (S-1/AC1-AC3, S-2/AC1-AC2) are covered by at least one test, and every covers entry points to a criterion that exists in split.md.
The change is web-only (the API is unchanged), so web unit tests in the existing PatientsPage test file are the cheapest level that proves it.
There is a negative test (TP-6), a zero boundary (TP-4) and a total-beyond-page boundary (TP-3). The singular '1 patient' boundary from the design is not tested. No new endpoint or field.
Tools and folder match the strategy (Vitest, jsdom, Testing Library, web/src/__tests__). Test titles are not prefixed with requirement IDs, which the strategy and the existing tests use.
Titles are short and concrete with clear expected outputs. TP-6 is mapped to S-1/AC1 even though it tests an error path that AC1 does not describe.

findings.text: The design specifies a singular form for exactly one match ('1 patient'), but no test covers that boundary. Only totals of 12, 0 and more than one page are tested.

cites.quote: Exactly one match reads "1 patient", the intent's Q-02 default.
TP-4 (unit): a total of 0 shows "0 patients". Covers S-2/AC1.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a unit test: a list response with total 1 shows '1 patient' (singular), traced to the design's Q-02 default.

findings.text: The strategy requires test names to start with their requirement ID, and the existing web tests follow this. The planned test titles carry no requirement ID prefix.

cites.quote: Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID (DOC-1, APT-4, ...).
HMS-2: an upcoming appointment still shows its doctor, linked to the appointment
A list response whose total is 12 shows '12 patients'

findings.suggested_fix: Prefix each test title with its ticket/REQ ID, e.g. 'LIVE-1 REQ-1: a total of 12 shows 12 patients'.

findings.text: The design says the count also follows the status filter, but TP-2 only exercises a change to the search text. No test shows the count updating when the filter changes.

cites.quote: so it follows the search text and the status filter with no extra request
TP-2 (unit): a search change refetches, and the count follows the new total.

findings.suggested_fix: Extend TP-2, or add a test, so a status filter change also refetches and the count follows the new total.

findings.text: TP-6 (a failed request shows the error and no count) is mapped to S-1/AC1, but AC1 only covers a successful search with 12 matches. The error behaviour is not part of any acceptance criterion.

cites.quote: TP-6 (unit, negative): a failed request shows the error and no count line. Covers S-1/AC1.
AC1: Given a search that 12 patients match, when the list is shown, then it shows "12 patients".

findings.suggested_fix: Mark TP-6 as a supplementary negative test rather than coverage of S-1/AC1, or trace it to a design behaviour.
